reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:5524 admit_once() calls _record_readiness_verdicts, which calls section_hold at :2407

findings.text: the fragment is written one directory deeper than the declared path docs/evidence/fragments/work-flows-to-the-lane/held-request-names-its-hold.html; reckon/evidence.py:745 composes fragment_dir/<node>.html and :757 globs *.html non-recursively, and reckon/crew/reports.py:2555 recognises a fragment only exactly one level under the plan directory, so this node's evidence never composes into the plan's cumulative record.

baseline_suite and after_suite carry prose sentences instead of the armed JSON observation the manifest contract requires; reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:1218 refuses a non-mapping after_suite ('records no after_suite observation of the delivered head'), so the run is refused at landing despite its gate having measured clean.
the head arm's log ends NODE_EXIT=0 rather than a bare EXIT=<code> line, and carries no '# command:' header, so promotion cannot read the head arm's exit status from the log the manifest names.

every queued hold is recorded with verdict 'held-on-readiness', including a hold on a declared section wait whose names are upstream refs; a reader selecting on the verdict classifies a genuine declared wait as a readiness hold, which is the mislabelling the node exists to remove.

record_section_hold's docstring claims 'a pointer that cannot be written is reported rather than assumed', but _record_pass_hold (:1442) swallows CrewError and returns None, record_section_hold returns True regardless, and dispatch.py:2354 ignores the return, so a failed pointer write leaves the dispatch answer claiming a hold the pointer does not carry.

_record_readiness_verdicts starts a fresh empty readonly cache per call, so the pass reads a plan once per readiness-held request rather than once per plan; the once-per-plan invariant asserted at tests/test_a_pass_computes_coverage_once.py:208 stays green only because its fixture holds no readiness request.
